This civil revision coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 JUDGMENT

This first appeal under Section 96 of C.P.C. has been filed against the judgment and decree dated 23/07/2004 passed by Additional District Judge, Karera, District Shivpuri in C.S. No.2-B/2001 who dismissed the suit of plaintiff for construction of shops demolished by defendants on the expenses of defendants and damage of Rs.2,00,000/-.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Karera, District Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The grounds of appeal are that in the suit filed for realization of damages of Rs.2,00,000/-
alleging that appellants are owner of the suit land bearing No.2723/1 measuring 1.881 hectors situated at Tahsil Karera District Shivpuri.
It is alleged that the property which is owned by the appellants is 75 feet in width towards East to West and 70 feet towards South to North measuring 5250 Sq.Ft.
Permission for construction was obtained by the appellants on 15/09/1995.

The appellants constructed seven shops and seven godown and residential accommodation on the suit property after leaving the space of 55 feet on the National Highway in which the appellants invested a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-.
3.

It is further submitted that vide notice dated 17/04/1998, the respondent No.3 alleged that appellants have made an encroachment on Government land measuring 40x15 meter and issued show cause notice to the effect as to why penalty of Rs.1,500/- should not be imposed.

The said notice dated 17/04/1998 was duly replied by the appellants on 14/05/1998 but after the reply neither any notice was issued nor any opportunity of hearing was given to the appellants by fixing any date in the matter.
On 14/07/1998 all of sudden the respondents demolished the shops.
At the time of demolition, the said shops were containing food grains.
In the circumstances the appellants claimed Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation alongwith interest.
4. The respondent No.2 to 5 submitted written statement whereas the other respondents did not file any written statement.
In the written statement submitted by respondent No.2 to 5 the allegations of the plaint were denied.
It was also denied that the shops were illegally removed and they were constructed on the property of appellants.
Any lose was denied.

On the basis of the pleadings, the Trial Court after framing the issues, recorded the evidence of both parties and after hearing the arguments, dismissed the suit holding that the appellants are not the owner of the land in dispute bearing Survey No. 2723/1 upon which the shops were constructed.
It was also held that the Brijmohan & Ors. vs Union Of India & Ors.

on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167844464/
2 appellants are encroachers and are not entitled for any relief.

5. Aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, this appeal has been filed on the ground that learned Trial Court committed an error in holding that suit property was not in the ownership of the appellants.
Shops were constructed on Survey No.2723/1.
The Trial Court failed to take into account revenue record for which certified copy was filed.
It is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1994(II) MPWN 133 that if certified copy of the revenue record has been produced then the same is required to be taken into consideration.
Permission for construction was also overlooked and no correct finding was given.
It can be presumed that without verifying the title of the appellants.
The Municipal Council could not have granted the permission.

Court also failed to take into consideration, the return filed by Executive Engineer National Highway, Shvipuri in W.P.No.1510/2000 in which it was specifically admitted that National Highway Act is not applicable to the Municipal areas and the construction on the land can be made after leaving open space of 15 meters from center point of the road on either sides.
Certified copy of this return was on record but the same was not taken into consideration.

It has been held in AIR 2002 Kerala Page 133 that certified copy of the return or statement submitted by one of the parties of the suit cannot be eschewed for want of proof of contents of the document.

6. It is further submitted that the learned Trial Court failed to take any note of the fact that no date of hearing was given to the appellants on the show cause notice dated 17/04/1998 and neither they were asked to produce the evidence regarding title of land and permission of Municipal Council for construction.
It is submitted that it was obligatory on the respondents to give an opportunity of hearing before passing the order.
In the order dated 13/07/1998, there is no mention that any opportunity of hearing for production of evidence was given to the appellants.
Further while passing the said order of ejectment and imposition of fine under Section 248 of M.P. Land Revenue Code, no time is given to remove the so called encroachment.
Therefore, respondents have acted in utter violation of principles of natural justice.
There was material contradictions in the statement of P.W.1 and P.W.2 (typographical error-- should have been D.W.1 and D.W.2) regarding the date of demolition of the construction.

D.W.1 has stated the said dated 13/07/1998 while D.W.2 has stated on 14/07/1998 which goes to show that there is manipulation in the documentary evidence by the respondents and the same was fabricated after demolition.
Therefore, on the above ground prayer is for allowing the appeal by setting aside the order of Trial Court.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the party ans perused the record.
8.
Question before this Court is as to whether any interference can be made to the judgment of the Trial Court.
9. Appellants have relied on Gunasekaran Vs. The Divisional Engineer, National Highways and Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
reported in (2021) 10 SCC 505 in which the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:-
"17.

A perusal of Section 26, bearing in mind the object with which the said law was enacted, leaves us in no manner of doubt, as regards power and procedure for the removal of any encroachment at a National Highway.
The appropriate law is the Act Brijmohan & Ors. vs Union Of India & Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

3 of 2002.
In other words, the show cause notices which have been issued and impugned in these cases are admittedly issued seeking shelter under Section 5 of the Act of 1956.

Power under Section 5 of the Act of 1956 does not extend as is made clear by the circumstances leading to the Act of 2002 and also the express provisions of the Act of 2002, in particular, Section 26 which provides for the procedure as also the power for causing the removal of encroachment in regard to National Highways.
Section 14 of the Act of 2002 confer a right of appeal to the Tribunal.

18. The upshot of the above discussion is that the show cause notices which have, in fact, been issued by the Civil Appeal No. 4946/2021 etc. officer clutching the power under Section 28 of the State Act, 2001, and which the learned senior counsel for the State seeks to rest under the provisions of the notification issued under Section 5 of the Act of 1956, are unauthorised.
As correctly observed by the High Court, one of the grounds on which show cause notices can be interfered with is the lack of jurisdiction of the authority.
This is one such case, where the authority to take action and the law under which such action can be taken are all found located in Act of 2002.
To be more specific, the provision of section 26 provides the statutory charter for setting in motion the proceedings to get rid of encroachment over National Highways.
19. The respondents do not have a case before us that the authority which has issued the impugned show cause notices in these cases is the authority contemplated under Section 26.
The authority contemplated in Section 26 is the Highway Authority constituted under Section 3 or any officer authorised by the Highway Authority.
20. Since no claim is raised based on powers under Section 26, we are constrained to interfere in the matter.
21. Accordingly, the impugned judgment is set aside.
The writ petitions are allowed.
The impugned show cause notices will stand set aside.
However, we make it crystal clear that this will be without prejudice to the competent Civil Appeal No. 4946/2021 etc. authority under Section 26 to take appropriate action as advised in law."

19. The judgment of Gunasekaran (supra) can be differentiated in the facts and circumstances of the present appeal before this Court.
In the case of Gunasekaran (supra) challenge was made to the show cause notice issued by respondent Divisional Engineer National Highway and others.
The matter relates to the State of Tamilnadu Highway Act, 2001.
Specifically Section 28(2)(ii) and enactment of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

Plaintiff/appellant has failed to prove that construction was as per the map or it was done within year and if it was not done so whether permission was extended by Nagar Parishad Karera, District Shivpuri, whether any written information was given regarding completion of work, plaintiff did not file any document regarding his ownership in fact during the cross-examination in para 14 has agreed that he has not filed registered sale-deed in fact at the stage of argument, he filed a Khasra of the year 2003-04 in which in column 3 name of the plaintiff has been entered as the possession but column 4 is blank which is for name of Bhumiswami (owner of the land), therefore, it seems that plaintiff has not come with all necessary facts and documents to prove his case that valid construction over the suit land in his ownership was demolished and what was the actual loss to him.
One ground of the appeal is that plaintiff was not called upon to produce the documents of title etc.
but plaintiff has not exhibited the reply filed by them in response to notice Ex.P-4 to Ex.P-6.

In fact in legal notice Ex.P-10 they have mentioned reply to the notice but it is the defendant department who has filed the reply submitted by the plaintiff as Ex.D-8, D-15 and D-22 and Ex.D-8,
D-15 and D-22 shows that no necessary documents on any sort have been annexed, on perusal of Trial Court record, it is found that reasonable opportunities have been given by the defendants to plaintiffs to submit their sanctioned map, documents of ownership etc., therefore, it is not a case where proper opportunity was not given but on the contrary a case where opportunity was given but for reasons best known to them (plaintiffs) they failed to avail that opportunity.

The conduct of party during the trial can also be taken judicial note of where during the trial also no documents of ownership were filed but on a different tangent permission to construct was filed, which is altogether a different aspect and belatedly at the stage of final argument a Khasra of the year 2003-04 was filed whereas the demolition was done in the year 1998 when Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002 and the revenue authorities and municipal authorities were empowered to remove encroachments as has been done in this case.

21. Accordingly, this first appeal fails and is hereby dismissed, judgment and decree of Trial Court is confirmed.
